chunks: What was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿĀmir, from Ḥajjāj al-Khashshāb, from Abī Hilāl, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “As for the menstruating woman, drink from what remains of her drink, but I do not like that wudu (ablution) be performed from it.”
Al-Shaykh, may Allah تعالى support him, said: Purification is not permissible with the leftover water of the disbelievers, including the polytheists, the Christians, the Magians, and the Sabeans.
That is indicated by His تعالى statement:

So He judged them to be impure by the apparent wording, and this entails the impurity of their leftovers through their contact with water. Also, the Muslims have unanimously agreed upon the impurity of the polytheists and the disbelievers in an unrestricted sense, and that too necessitates the impurity of their leftovers and also indicates it.

key_terms.أَسْآرِ الْكُفَّارِ: the leftover liquids or vessels of the disbelievers after their use
key_terms.فَضْلِ شَرَابِهَا: what remains of her drink after she has drunk from it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use leftover water from a menstruating woman or from disbelievers for wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This text distinguishes between the leftover drink of a menstruating woman and that of disbelievers. It permits drinking from her leftover drink while expressing dislike for using it for wudu (ablution), and it further states that purification with the leftovers of certain disbelievers is not permissible, citing the Qur'anic declaration of impurity regarding the polytheists.
